justification: The evidence shows the system maintains fairly high accuracy under several predefined perturbations and formatting variations, and it also detects many out-of-distribution documents. This supports some operational robustness beyond nominal conditions. However, the evidence is limited to the stated tests and does not fully demonstrate robustness across the whole deployment context, especially since the out-of-distribution mechanism missed 73 of 1,200 excluded-class documents and the available information does not cover other relevant operating conditions.
evidence_used: With 10% randomly removed non-critical fields, accuracy was 93.7%.
With the predefined OCR degradation transformation, accuracy was 92.1%.
Across the predefined formatting-variation set, accuracy ranged from 91.6% to 94.8%.
Out-of-distribution test set contained 1,200 documents from document classes excluded from training; 1,127 were flagged by the out-of-distribution mechanism.
Validation protocol contains three predefined perturbation tests; corresponding accuracies were 92.8%, 90.9%, and 93.4%.
A separate validation team reproduced the reported tests.
limitations: Evidence is restricted to predefined perturbation, formatting, and out-of-distribution tests described in the case.
No evidence is provided for robustness across the full range of real deployment conditions.
The out-of-distribution mechanism did not flag all excluded-class samples.
Nominal validation accuracy alone is not sufficient to establish operational robustness, so the conclusion cannot be fully supported from the provided material.
